articles.title: US Open tennis 2026 men’s semi-final: Frances Tiafoe v Ben Shelton – live
articles.summary: Updates from the second men’s semi-final in New York Zverev takes out Khachanov in straight sets to make final Andrew Lawrence: in praise of five-set tennis | Mail Bryan.
body: Shelton holds at love, crushing his 11th and 12th aces of the night. Tiafoe will serve to stay in the third set.
Tiafoe holds at love. Much-needed. Shelton had won 10 of the previous 11 points before that game.

Another scratchy service game for Tiafoe and he’s quickly down love-40, gifting Shelton three break-point chances. And he needs only one! Shelton rips a cross-court backhand winner to finish off a 10-shot rally and secure the break for his first lead of the night.

With Shelton serving at 15-all, he casually steps up and pounds a 158mph serve out wide, which would be the fastest ever recorded serve at an ATP event, besting the previous mark of 157.2 mph set by John Isner at the 2016 Davis Cup. Well then. He gets to 40-15 before Tiafoe pushes it to deuce. But Shelton wins two quick points from there to nail down the hold.

articles.title: ‘This is my moment’: Taylor Townsend’s road comes full circle with US Open triumph
articles.summary: The 30-year-old once denied USTA funding returned to Arthur Ashe Stadium to complete her career doubles grand slam alongside Kateřina Siniaková. The cheers swelled from Arthur Ashe Stadium as Taylor Townsend approached the microphone on court.
body: A day after being denied an American rooting interest in the women’s singles final and rushing for the exits in response, the Ashe crowd had reason to stick around and drink in the moment: the Chicago native and her partner, Kateřina Siniaková of the Czech Republic, had just defeated the all-American team of Ashlyn Krueger and Robin Montgomery 5-7, 6-0, 6-2 in Friday’s women’s doubles final. With the victory, Siniaková became a two-time career doubles slam champion while Townsend joined the club for the first time.

articles.title: Zverev through to third Grand Slam final in a row
articles.summary: Alexander Zverev beats Karen Khachanov at the US Open to reach a third Grand Slam final in a row and continue his bid for a second major of the year.
body: The top seed put in a commanding performance to beat the Russian 6-3 7-6 (9-7) 7-6 (8-6).
Germany's Zverev is the favourite in New York after ending his long wait for a Grand Slam title with his French Open triumph in June.
He reached the Wimbledon final in July, losing in four sets to world number one Jannik Sinner.
The 29-year-old will play either eighth seed Ben Shelton or 11th seed Frances Tiafoe in Sunday's showpiece, with the two Americans set to meet in Friday's night session.

articles.title: Alexander Zverev holds his nerve against Karen Khachanov to reach US Open final
articles.summary: Zverev wins 6-3, 7-6 (7), 7-6 (6) German reaches third straight grand slam final. About 107 minutes into men’s semi-final day on Arthur Ashe Stadium, there was finally a touch of tension radiating from the court.
body: There was a time when Zverev might have faltered under such pressure, but he has won too many big matches this year to allow such a small surge from a lower-ranked opponent to scare him. Zverev composed himself and he quickly regained control, navigating a second tense tie-break in similar fashion as he moved to within one match of winning a second career grand slam title in his last three major appearances by defeating Khachanov 6-3, 7-6 (7), 7-6 (6).

Zverev has now reached three consecutive grand slam finals for the first time in his career, with the German following up his maiden grand slam title at Roland Garros with a first Wimbledon final this summer. Zverev reached his first grand slam final here back in 2020, losing to Dominic Thiem in a dramatic five-set match during a closed Covid-era tournament after leading by two sets and serving for the title. He will now compete for the title in his sixth grand slam final.

articles.title: Nicola Olyslagers finds silver lining in high jump jackpot at Ultimate Championship
articles.summary: Australian earns biggest payday of career with second behind Mahuchikh. Kurtis Marschall finishes fourth after Armand Duplantis in pole vault. Nicola Olyslagers has had the best worst night of her career after missing out on becoming a new “Ultimate” athletics high jump champion, only to learn to…
body: Australia’s world champion managed to only clear 1.95m on the first night of World Athletics’ inaugural Ultimate Championship in Budapest on Friday (Saturday AEST), struggling with her approach on a difficult surface on a cold night as Ukraine’s Olympic champ Yaroslava Mahuchikh beat her to the title with a 1.99m leap.

Olyslagers’ runner’s-up spot earned her US$75,000 (AU$105,000) – US$5,000 more than she pocketed for winning the world title last year – as part of the record $US10 million ($14m) prize pot for the streamlined new event that World Athletics hopes will attract a host of new fans.
Only when speaking to reporters afterwards did Olyslagers realise just what she would be taking home.
“What? Really? I genuinely thought it was just first prize got the 150k and second was like 10,000,” she said. “You are the bearer of good news. That’s fantastic.”

articles.title: Glitzy innovations but Duplantis still wins - new Ultimate Championship begins
articles.summary: The Ultimate Championship is posed as something different in athletics, but some things stay the same - pole vault star Armand Duplantis taking centre stage.
body: A bright pink sandpit and a pitch black infield. A brand new trophy and historic prize money.

As the inaugural competition's official song, which two-time Olympic champion Duplantis wrote and recorded, was played to a sell-out crowd of more than 20,000, all eyes fell on the Swedish 26-year-old as, yet again, it was just him against the world record.
Duplantis had already secured the title of inaugural champion in the event he has long dominated, and his $150,000 (£110,000) slice of the record $10m (£7.4m) prize pot on offer.

While he was unable to clear 6.32m and set the 16th world record of his remarkable career, an entertaining battle with Greek challenger Emmanouil Karalis had provided the blockbuster finale to the opening night of action in Budapest.

articles.title: Like Benzema & as good as Haaland - Alonso on Joao Pedro
articles.summary: Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso says striker Joao Pedro is similar stylistically to his former Real Madrid team-mate Karim Benzema and is at a comparable level to Manchester City's Erling Haaland.
body: Xabi Alonso says Chelsea striker Joao Pedro is similar in style to his former Real Madrid team-mate Karim Benzema - and at a comparable level to Manchester City 's Erling Haaland.
The Brazil international, 24, has scored twice and provided two assists in his first three games of the season - and was named the Premier League's Player of the Month on Friday.
It was the first time Joao Pedro has won the award as he finished ahead of team-mate Cole Palmer, who was Chelsea 's previous recipient in September 2024.
When asked whether the forward could be compared to the prolific Haaland, who won last season's Premier League Golden Boot with 27 goals, Blues boss Alonso said: "I would say yes.

articles.title: No. 18 FSU soccer ties NC State 2-2 in ACC opener
articles.summary: No. 18 Florida State hosted NC State Friday evening in its first ACC matchup of the season, ending the night with a 2-2 draw. The Seminoles move to 4-1-2 on the season, while the Wolfpack move to 7-0-2.
body: FSU goalkeeper Kate Ockene entered the matchup after being named ACC Goalkeeper of the Week for her performance against Rice on Sunday.

Florida State’s starting lineup featured Ockene in goal; Olivia Page and Claire Rain on the back line; Shaneil Buckley, Peyton McGovern, Joelle Jung and Sam Erbach in the midfield; and Nyah Rose, Tanner Strickland, Wrianna Hudson and Ryder Ajeto up front.
The Seminoles were still without Bridget Mutipula, Janet Okeke and Nyanya Touray, who are competing in the FIFA U-20 Women’s World Cup.
NC State wasted little time getting on the board. Erica Roberts scored just 1:37 into the match to give the Wolfpack an early 1-0 lead.

articles.title: Wigan beat Catalans to lift sixth League Leaders' Shield
articles.summary: Wigan Warriors win a sixth League Leaders' Shield as they beat Catalans Dragons to wrap up top spot in Super League heading into the play-offs.
body: Wigan Warriors won a sixth League Leaders' Shield as they ran in nine tries to beat Catalans Dragons and carry on their remarkable run of form heading into the Super League play-offs.

Matt Peet's side, who were trophyless in 2025 off the back of their quadruple-winning 2024 campaign, have now won two pieces of silverware, having lifted the Challenge Cup in May, and are now two games away from a treble.
Harry Smith and Ugo Tison exchanged tries early on, but Liam Marshall, Brad O'Neill and Liam Farrell put Wigan in control at the break.

Austin Daniel and Jai Field continued Wigan's scoring streak, while Zach Eckersley, Adam Keighran and Marshall's second wrapped up a thumping 16th win in a row, with Alexis Lis scoring a fine consolation try for Les Dracs in the closing stages.

articles.title: Bucs DB Zyon McCollum gives Joe Burrow and the Bengals some bulletin-board material
articles.summary: Every sport has its unwritten rules, and one of the most universal is simple: Don’t give your opponent “bulletin-board material.” Don’t say something that can be printed out, slapped on a wall, and pointed to by a coach looking for a little extra motivation.
body: In the end, almost anything can be twisted into locker-room material in one way or another. When Tampa Bay Buccaneers defensive back Zyon McCollum was asked how he felt about playing against one of the most talented offenses in the league in Week 1, he had plenty of ways he could have answered.

“We’re going to have opportunities, guaranteed opportunities,” he said when asked about his Week 1 opponents. “I mean, they want to get their season started off right. They want to get in rhythm early, so the ball is guaranteed to go in the air. And a ball in the air belongs to us. You know, that’s the mentality that we have. That’s what we’re going into the game thinking. We know we’re going to get tested early, so it’s an incredible opportunity for us.
“There will be no better feeling than when we take away three, four interceptions.”

articles.title: Final Eagles injury report ahead of Week 1 game vs. Commanders
articles.summary: After watching their 2025 NFL season get derailed by injuries – in addition to the play-calling faux pas of Kevin Patullo – the Philadelphia Eagles find themselves relatively unscathed heading into Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season.
body: Final Eagles injury report ahead of Week 1 game vs. Commanders appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

Now granted, that can change in a hurry, as the Seattle Seahawks and New England Patriots quickly learned in their Wednesday night Super Bowl rematch, but with their final injury report submitted before Week 1, only two players appear: star free agent edge rusher Jonathan Greenard, who is officially out, and rookie tight end Eli Stowers, who is questionable to make his NFL debut against the Washington Commanders.

While Greenard won’t be on the field in Week 1 alongside Nolan Smith, Jalyx Hunt, Jalen Carter, Jordan Davis and company, it sounds like his absence won’t be an extended one, as he said he was “ close ” heading into Week 1.

“That’s not for me to decide. I feel good, though,” Greenard said on Thursday. “I will say I feel I’m in a good spot, just to know that. I know that I’m working every day to continue to try to get this thing stronger. We’re close, I know that.”
